# tongue

> On-device language identification for short text. Returns an ISO language code,
> ranked alternatives with probabilities, and an explicit "not sure" signal.
> 84 languages, one 2 MB model, three SDKs that return identical answers.
> No network call and no inference runtime.

This file exists for coding agents integrating the SDK. Everything below is
verified against version 0.1.2; each snippet is executed in CI.

## Facts

- Languages: 84 codes. 59 decoded by the model, 25 settled by script alone.
- Model: 2,104,940 bytes, int8, bundled in every package. Nothing is downloaded.
- Latency: ~17 microseconds per detection (Node 23, Apple M-series).
- Detection performs no I/O and no network access.
- Licence: source-available, free below a threshold, commercial above it.
- Repository: https://github.com/Desert-Ant-Labs/tongue

## Install

- Swift: `.package(url: "https://github.com/Desert-Ant-Labs/tongue.git", from: "0.1.2")`
- Kotlin: `implementation("ai.desertant:tongue:0.1.2`
- JavaScript: `npm install @desert-ant-labs/tongue`

## Minimal usage

Swift:

    import Tongue
    let tongue = try Tongue()
    tongue.detect("kann ich das haben").language   // "de"

Kotlin (pass a Context on Android; omit it on a bare JVM):

    import ai.desertant.tongue.Tongue
    val tongue = Tongue.bundled(context)
    tongue.detect("kann ich das haben").language   // "de"

JavaScript (Node):

    import { Tongue } from "@desert-ant-labs/tongue";
    const tongue = await Tongue.load();
    tongue.detect("kann ich das haben").language;  // "de"

JavaScript (browser) — you must serve the model yourself and pass `from`:

    const tongue = await Tongue.load({ from: "/models/tongue" });

## Return shape

`detect(text, topK = 3)` returns:

- `language`: top ISO code, or null on empty input
- `candidates`: ranked list, each with `language` and `probability`
- `reliability`: one of `confident`, `likely`, `tentative`, `empty`
- `isTooCloseToCall`: true when the top two are within 0.12
- `normalized`: the text as the model saw it
- `route.verdict`: `decisive`, `narrowing`, or `ambiguous`

Note: the verdict enum lives on `route`, not directly on the detection.

## Integration requirements that commonly break builds

1. Swift needs 6.2 tooling (Xcode 26+). An older Xcode resolves the package and
   then fails to build it, because a transitive dependency's manifest declares
   swift-tools 6.2.
2. In a browser, `Tongue.load()` without `from` resolves against the page URL and
   fetches `index.html` on a single-page app. Copy both model files into a static
   directory and pass `from` pointing at it:

       cp node_modules/@desert-ant-labs/tongue/dist/tongue_int8.bin \
          node_modules/@desert-ant-labs/tongue/dist/tongue_meta.json \
          public/models/tongue/

   Do not derive the base from a Vite `?url` import: `load` takes one directory,
   and Vite inlines `tongue_meta.json` (2.4 kB, under the 4 kB inline limit) as a
   `data:` URI while emitting the 2 MB `.bin` as a file, so the two disagree.
3. On Android, pass the `Context` to `Tongue.bundled(context)`. Without it there
   is nowhere durable to store the usage device id.
4. The npm package is ESM-only. `require()` works natively on Node 20.19+. For
   TypeScript in a CommonJS project, set `"moduleResolution": "nodenext"`
   (TS 5.8+); the older `node16` setting fails with TS1479 even though the
   runtime works. On Node older than 20.19, use dynamic `import()`.

## Correct handling of uncertainty

Short text is often genuinely undecidable. Do not present `tentative` as an
answer, and when `isTooCloseToCall` is true, show both candidates rather than
picking one. `"la casa"` is equally Italian and Spanish; `"Samsung Galaxy"` is
not language at all.

## Privacy

Detection never touches the network and no text ever leaves the device. A
separate licence-metering event reports a generated UUID, the app identifier and
a detection count — never text or results. Disable with the environment variable
`DAL_USAGE_DISABLED=1`, or `globalThis.__dalUsageDisabled = "1"` in a browser.
